sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company designs/manufactures FRP doors, frames, biodigesters and other engineered composite products; undertakes sewage/effluent treatment supply, installation and commissioning, with some operation/maintenance; and sells fire doors. FY26 management mix is Aqua 49.45%, FRP43.04%, Fire 7.51%. This is a hybrid manufacturing/project business: order wins do not equal cash earnings, and the same facility-utilization measure cannot safely scale all revenue lines. [S1 MD&A; S6 pp 8–17]

Aqua customers buy compliance, treatment and installation; FRP buyers buy durability, low maintenance and customized sizes. Government and private infrastructure offer demand, but tenders, milestones, retention and acceptance can delay cash. Audited services revenue is only ₹0.2138 cr of ₹13.6398 cr, so an O&M opportunity is not yet evidence that the whole business is a recurring annuity. Procurement combines resins/composite inputs, outsourced production/labor and equipment; supplier concentration/contractual pass-through details are ND. [S1 p 57]

Management’s 60% non-government/40% government end-user chart is not a legal counterparty exposure chart. Om Ventures is the related intermediary/legal debtor for 62.1% of sales and 70.4% of receivables. The company took over Om’s business in August 2021 while continuing legacy contracts; this explains some connected activity, but does not make the collection exposure disappear. No reliable current top-five independent-customer or supplier list was found. [S1 pp 30,62; S5; S6 p 17]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Strengths are an established Goa execution footprint, FRP engineering and fabrication experience, technology access and customer references. Installation/service may create local convenience and qualification benefits. DRDO/TIFAC/IISc-associated work and other partners are evidence of access and collaboration, not proof of exclusive intellectual property or a statutory monopoly. No measured price premium, customer switching-cost cohort, retention rate, patent-enforced economics or segment ROIC was available. [S1 MD&A; S5 Business; S6 pp 12–16]

Comparable business context, not a multiple-based target:

| Peer | Relevant overlap | Critical difference / use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VA Tech Wabag | Municipal/industrial water EPC and O&M | Broader international project and concession models; compare execution/collections discipline, not award its multiple to EP. [S11 PDF p 4] |
| Enviro Infra Engineers | Design, build, commission and long O&M water/wastewater projects | Larger turnkey/municipal contracts and 1–15 year O&M scope; not a FRP/firedoor equivalent. [S12 PDF pp 4,7] |
| Ion Exchange | Water/wastewater systems, services and consumables | Resins/membranes/consumables and broader technology mix create different recurrence/economics. [S13] |

No synchronized peer share prices, debt, lease normalization or segment valuation set has been verified. Thus no numerical peer-discount assertion is used. The 7×base exit EBITDA is an analyst normalization assumption, below EP’s own conservative current 7.48×cross-check, not a borrowed large-cap premium. MOAT 4 reflects unproven structural differentiation; it is not an assertion the products lack utility.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The relevant capital test is not today’s ROCE. Operating invested capital includes net working capital after operating liabilities/gratuity, net PPE/intangibles, all CWIP and other operating non-current assets including the ₹2 cr related lease deposit. Cash, financing balances and income-tax assets/liabilities are excluded. Normalized NOPAT=(PBT+finance−all other income)×75%. The 25% rate is an analytical normalization, not a claim about statutory tax election. [S1 pp 50–58; S3 pp 18–25]

| ₹cr | FY23 | FY26 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net ONWC after gratuity | 5.22 | 9.72 | 4.50 |
| Net PPE/intangibles+CWIP | 0.3334 | 0.8535 | 0.5201 |
| Other operating NCA | 2.1275 | 2.1146 | −0.0129 |
| Operating IC | 7.6831 | 12.6883 | 5.0052 |
| Normalized NOPAT | 0.6380 | 1.6020 | 0.9640 |

Incremental ROIC FY23–26=₹0.963975 cr/₹5.0052 cr=19.26%. The investment bridge reconciles: capex ₹0.8349 cr less D&A ₹0.3144 cr gives ₹0.5205 cr; net asset movement ₹0.5201 cr differs ₹0.0004 cr(disposal/loss/rounding). Add ₹4.4980 cr ONWC and−₹0.0129 cr NCA change to reach ₹5.0052 cr. All CWIP and unchanged Om deposit remain in the denominator. Funding-side IC independently reconciles within ₹0.02 lakh historical rounding. [model_results.json, cap_bridge]

A reasoned nominal INR capital-cost comparison range is 13–17%, an analyst risk range for small project/manufacturing economics, not a verified market WACC and not the 15% equity hurdle relabeled. 19.26% is encouraging but does not establish durable excess returns: FY26 average IC ROIC is 12.86%; endpoint profit recovery and assumed collectibility drive incremental accrual returns. No project cash IRR or mature/new cohort substitute is evidenced. Five-year incremental ROIC is NM because FY21 precedes takeover. CAP 6 reflects this mixed evidence, not a neutral score filled in for missing analysis.

The runway includes smaller private industrial/hospitality STPs, FRP substitution and select municipal work. The 26 September 70 KLD Beleza order is ₹0.9204 cr due 30 April 2027; the 29 September water-body collaboration has no upfront consideration and no guaranteed revenue. Other project references are not summed into an unexecuted backlog because recognition, GST, retention and overlap are unreconciled. S6 p 16 states manufacturing capacity 2.0 lakh sq ft in FY26–27 and 70%/1.4 lakh sq ft utilization. This is not evidence of a new 2 lakh sq ft building or a complete revenue capacity bridge. Additional working capital, not simply adding machines, is the likely scale constraint. [S6–S8]

GQS raw 5.90 is capped 5.00 because persistent CASH 3. Profitable growth is possible; self-funded cash compounding is not demonstrated.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters held 70.08% at 31 March 2026: Leena Kamat 64.93%, Rajkumar Kamat 3.99%, Nimisha 0.85%, Ashma 0.31%. Issued capital 16,81,500 shares was unchanged FY23–26. Rajkumar’s ₹0.18 cr remuneration was unchanged FY24–26; interest-free director loan declined from ₹0.8275 cr to ₹0.7715 cr during FY26. These are favorable minority-alignment counterpoints, but not proof all future group transactions are fair. The official 19 October master also confirms 1,681,500 issued shares. Promoter holdings remain dated March; current pledge status and complete corporate-action history are unverified. Secondary zero-pledge reports are not promoted to primary facts. [S1 pp 54,62,64; S17, S18]

AOC-2 was inspected visually across PDF pp 30–32, not inferred from extracted text. Om rent ₹3.13 lakh and sales ₹846.97 lakh sit directly under section 1 “not at arm’s length basis”; Business Nirvana rent ₹9.50 lakh continues that section. Section 2 on p 32 separately states no material arm’s-length transactions. No NIL marker intervenes before the Om rows. The form explains legacy Om contracts after business takeover and board/member approvals 5/7 July 2021. This is a verified disclosure classification, not an allegation of diversion. The notice’s arm’s-length pricing assertion concerns the separate proposed land purchase, not proof the Om classification is incorrect. [S1 pp 30–32; S2B p 12]

FY25 AGM notice proposed purchase of the leased Bicholim plots and possible Kundaim industrial plots from Leena Kamat up to ₹5.5 cr; timing was not finalized and pricing was asserted arm’s length. Authorization/proposal is not a completed transaction or committed cash outflow. FY26 CARO says no owned immovable property at March end; ₹0.4082 cr land/civil/electrification CWIP does not establish title purchase. Base cash flow does not charge ₹5.5 cr. A separate stress does, with no assumed refund/netting of existing Om deposit. Current status, valuation report, member approval outcome and payment terms are open. [S2B p 12; S1 pp 44,56]

IPO ₹6.3504 cr was all fresh capital, not OFS. Latest use table lists working capital ₹1.5118 cr, Leena loan repayment ₹0.8 cr, lease deposit ₹2 cr, general corporate purposes ₹1.4886 cr and issue cost ₹0.5105 cr, all marked utilized. These sum ₹6.3109 cr, ₹0.0395 cr short of gross; this matches estimated ₹0.55 cr issue cost less actual ₹0.5105 cr. Allocation of that saving is unclear, not proof of misuse. Do not assume additional IPO cash or ignore the gap. [S1 p 64; S5 Objects]

The unmodified audit, operating audit trail, positive IFC opinion, no reported fraud/default and auditor’s explicitly limited 12-month liability assessment are meaningful positive evidence. They do not guarantee commercial fairness or collection. Real FY26 earnings/project progress coexist with old plant CWIP and unreconciled capacity/project milestones. GOV 4/EXEC 5, not an automatic governance Fail. [S1 pp 39–49]

Opening cash availability: ₹2.1535 cr reported includes current/hand ₹1.2265 cr, RD ₹0.1373 cr, FD ₹0.7897 cr. All RD/FD are excluded strictly pending release/encumbrance proof; this does not assert all are pledged. SIDBI note says 25% of original ₹2.15 cr loan held in FD, minimum indication ₹0.5375 cr. sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The ₹92 reference is a stale secondary last trade, not an executable quote. With 1,681,500 issued shares it implies market capitalization ₹15.4698 cr. Reported P/E10.61×; normalized P/E11.48×; P/B 1.28×; conservative EV/core EBITDA 7.48×. Current EV adds all ₹2.3956 cr debt and subtracts only ₹1.1265 cr available excess cash after the ₹0.10 cr operating reserve. Restricted/unverified deposits and the operating lease deposit are not separately added. One-year after-finance owner-cash yield is 6.87%, but the three-year average is −2.82%. None of these multiples establishes intrinsic value. [S1, S10; model_results.json]

Model structure: five synthetic annual periods ending 19 October 2027–2031, anchored in FY26 run-rate economics and the March balance sheet. This is not a verified October balance sheet. Starting available cash ₹1.2265 cr; starting net ONWC ₹9.7202 cr. D&A is 0.8% of revenue; capex has a ₹0.20 cr annual floor. Cash tax is 25% of positive forecast PBT; losses receive no immediate tax credit. Interest is 8.9% of average bank principal plus ₹0.05 cr other finance costs each year; no return on bank deposits is assumed. No dividends, new ordinary borrowing or unverified facility is used. Indian-GAAP lease rent remains an expense, not a capitalized lease or EBITDA add-back.

Bank principal schedule ₹0.526/0.526/0.526/0.0461/0 cr is an analytical maturity stress anchored in current maturities, not a lender-certified amortization schedule. The ₹0.7715 cr interest-free director loan is repaid in year one in strict cases because repayment terms are unknown; this is not an assertion it is contractually due then. Net old income tax ₹0.4121 cr and old interest ₹0.0091 cr are paid once in year one. Opening operating liabilities already reduce ONWC and are not deducted again. Required minimum cash ₹0.10 cr is retained and not added to terminal enterprise value. [claims_ledger.json]

| Case | Growth path | EBIT margin path | ONWC/revenue path | Capex/revenue | Exit EV/EBITDA | Peak net top-up ₹cr | Ordinary IRR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bear | -15%, 0%, 5%, 5%, 5% | 8%, 9%, 10%, 11%, 11% | 90%, 90%, 87%, 84%, 82% | 2.50% | 5 | 1.00 | NS: unfunded |
| base | 10%, 10%, 10%, 10%, 10% | 14.5%, 14.5%, 14.5%, 14.5%, 14.5% | 72%, 72%, 72%, 72%, 72% | 3.00% | 7 | 0.97 | NS: unfunded |
| bull | 18%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 10% | 16%, 16.5%, 17%, 17%, 17% | 68%, 65%, 62%, 60%, 58% | 4.00% | 9 | 0.81 | NS: unfunded |

Strict base annual bridge, ₹cr. Negative cash is an infeasibility diagnostic, never an assumption that the business operates without funding:

| Year | Revenue | PAT | ΔONWC | Capex | Principal | Old claims | Cash, before rescue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 15.00 | 1.50 | 1.08 | 0.45 | 1.30 | 0.42 | -0.40 |
| 2 | 16.50 | 1.70 | 1.08 | 0.50 | 0.53 | 0.00 | -0.67 |
| 3 | 18.15 | 1.92 | 1.19 | 0.54 | 0.53 | 0.00 | -0.87 |
| 4 | 19.97 | 2.13 | 1.31 | 0.60 | 0.05 | 0.00 | -0.53 |
| 5 | 21.97 | 2.35 | 1.44 | 0.66 | 0.00 | 0.00 | -0.10 |

All three growth cases have an annual cash shortfall. Consequently ordinary terminal equity values, per-share prices and IRRs are null. The peak top-up includes restoring the ₹0.10 cr minimum buffer, not an undisclosed cash facility. Merely delaying the director loan until year five still leaves the base case short by ₹0.1964 cr. Adding ₹0.3895 cr of unverified deposit liquidity still leaves ₹0.5773 cr short. Neither is treated as committed funding. In contrast, a restrained path of 0% then four years of 3% revenue growth, 14.5% EBIT margin and 1% capex/revenue with the same capex floor remains funded, minimum cash ₹0.6714 cr, and returns 5.81%. This is positive survival counterevidence, not the supported growth base.

Separate, expressly uncommitted rescue illustration: inject equity whenever necessary at ₹46/share, with 2% issue costs, retaining all operating assumptions and paying the director loan. This is a dilution stress, not a proposed financing transaction or a claim that such pricing meets issuance rules. Shares are modeled continuously for sensitivity, with insignificant actual share-rounding differences. No rescue has been approved or evidenced. Gross proceeds enter cash once and new shares dilute current holders once:

| Uncommitted rescue | Y5 revenue ₹cr | Y5 EBITDA ₹cr | Y5 cash ₹cr | Gross equity raise ₹cr | Dilution | Terminal price ₹ | 5-year IRR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bear | 13.42 | 1.58 | 1.28 | 1.03 | 11.70% | 47.77 | -12.28% |
| base | 21.97 | 3.36 | 0.87 | 0.99 | 11.31% | 128.15 | 6.85% |
| bull | 26.91 | 4.79 | 3.12 | 0.82 | 9.61% | 247.98 | 21.93% |

Terminal EV = year-five core EBITDA × exit multiple. Equity = EV + cash less the operating reserve − remaining bank/director debt. Taxes and principal already paid are not subtracted a second time; the Om deposit and excluded RD/FD are not added. All annual residuals reconcile to zero. Base terminal proceeds, not a separate dividend stream, contain retained cash.

Reverse expectations: at 10% annual growth, 72% ONWC and 7× EBITDA exit, a 15% return requires approximately 18.13% EBIT margin throughout, versus FY26 core 15.66%. At 14.5% EBIT margin, it instead requires 10.21× terminal EBITDA. These calculations include rescue dilution where required. A growth-only search from 0–75% produces no 15% solution: working-capital needs and dilution make return non-monotonic; the best scanned result is about 7.06% at 13% growth. There is no fabricated root or assumption that faster sales always increase per-share value.

Two-way sensitivity below is conditional rescue IRR; ordinary IRR is null in every cell. Rows vary revenue growth, columns terminal EV/EBITDA, holding base margins/working-capital ratios:

| Growth | 5× | 7× | 9× |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.00% | -0.08% | 6.18% | 11.24% |
| 10.00% | 0.15% | 6.85% | 12.20% |
| 14.00% | -0.11% | 6.84% | 12.35% |
| 18.00% | -1.14% | 5.75% | 11.20% |
| 22.00% | -1.99% | 4.84% | 10.24% |

Assumption-dependent base-rescue entry prices for 12%/15%/18% hurdles are ₹72.72/₹63.71/₹56.02. This ₹56–73 range is not a buy limit or observable fair value; it assumes the same hypothetical ₹46 financing price, not a dynamically repriced rescue. Equal entry and exit execution haircuts of 2%/5%/10% reduce the base illustration to 6.00%/4.74%/2.65%. Actual spread/impact is unknown. No personal taxes or portfolio-specific charges are included. R remains NS and P is 4, rather than scoring the hypothetical rescue as a funded investment opportunity.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Impairment risk: High. The linked path is delayed Om and independent-customer collections → longer working-capital lock-up → weaker utilization/margins → cash shortfall while debt, tax and payroll remain due → unfavorable recapitalization or curtailed operations. A small quoted market value does not subordinate those claims to ordinary shareholders. The central thesis-break variable is documented collectibility, not a daily share-price move.

The ordinary bear case cannot fund its assumed path and therefore has no IRR or executable terminal price. Its peak net funding top-up is ₹1.005 cr. Only after the explicitly uncommitted rescue does a terminal price of ₹47.77 emerge, -48.07% versus entry, with 11.70% dilution and -12.28% annualized return. This is a conditional recovery illustration, not a lower bound on loss; absent funding, shareholder recovery could be worse.

Independent asset-value cross-check: reported book equity ₹12.053 cr or ₹71.68/share is not cash backing. Haircuts of 30% to the Om receivable, 25% to its deposit, 10% to other receivables and 20% to inventory reduce equity by ₹3.619 cr to ₹8.434 cr, about ₹50.16/share, 45.5% below ₹92. These are analyst stress rates, not asserted defaults, and realization costs/timing could reduce recovery further. This impairment calculation is separate from cash-flow scenarios and is not deducted again from their terminal value.

If the optional ₹5.5 cr land authorization were to become an immediate purchase with no deposit refund, strict base peak top-up would rise to ₹6.467 cr. This is not a committed obligation inferred from an authorization. A documented deposit offset could alter that case; no such offset is assumed. A current lender schedule, enforceable director standstill or proved cash release may materially improve funding. [S1, S2B]

Contrary evidence must remain visible: FY26 collections improved, Om receivables fell, debt declined and audit opinions were unmodified. A funded low-growth path exists in the model. These facts rule out calling the company proven insolvent on the assessed evidence. They do not establish a safe 15% investment return or a cash-generative compounder.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Five-year multibagger feasibility is speculative / unsupported, not the central investment case. With unchanged normalized earnings margin, diluted shares and P/E, price growth requires proportional revenue growth. The decomposition is an arithmetic requirement, not a projection; terminal cash and financing need a separate enterprise-to-equity model.

| Five-year price outcome | Required price CAGR | Revenue at same margin/P/E ₹cr | Extra ONWC at 72% ₹cr | Revenue if exit P/E25% lower ₹cr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5× | 37.97% | 68.20 | 39.28 | 90.93 |
| 10× | 58.49% | 136.40 | 88.39 | 181.86 |

Those ₹68–136 cr revenue scales are far above today’s ₹13.64 cr. Even before extra fixed assets and contingencies, the working-capital requirement is substantial. A credible case would require independent-customer expansion, materially better collections, verified capacity/project delivery and funding that does not dilute away per-share gains. Neither a tiny market cap, technology-partner logos nor one new order proves this. Accessible market share and plant/project throughput at that scale are ND; no precise success probability or distant price target is assigned. [S1, S6–S8]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Research priority: cash conversion, related-party collection and current funding first; liquidity implementation second. BQS 4.7/GQS 5.0 remain eligible for Medium-confidence business-quality comparisons. IAS is NS and excluded from investment-attractiveness ranking; no numeric matrix cell is forced from the 2.62–6.67 missing-data bound. This is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate: GOV, MOAT, CASH, BAL and aggregate quality do not meet the framework thresholds.

Before investment consideration: reconcile October cash and committed facilities; obtain enforceable debt/director maturity terms; independently verify material collections and aging; clarify land exposure and small disclosure differences; recheck the dated official 500-share lot and obtain complete restrictions, share-claim and liquidity records. A lower price alone does not cure these gates. An existing holding is a review-for-evidence case, not an unconditional sell instruction; no holding, cost basis, size, taxes or urgency is supplied.

The liquidity test is particularly restrictive. The 20/60-session NSE-calendar proxy contains only 5/26 observed BSE secondary trade rows; 15/34 dates remain UNKNOWN, never zero. Observed-only mean close×volume proxies are ₹2.18 lakh/₹1.77 lakh and medians ₹1.35 lakh/₹1.39 lakh. They are not actual traded value or complete-window averages. Full-window mean/median, zero-day counts, conservative capacity and exit days are NS.

The official 19 October 2026 interoperable security master verifies a 500-share lot, 1,681,500 issued shares and normal-market eligibility for the exact ISIN, under BSE-listed code 2. It does not establish an NSE listing. Status 6 denotes price discovery/pre-open, not permanent suspension. The dated ₹73.60–110.40 price range is metadata, not bid/ask depth or an observed trade. [S17, S18]

At the verified 500-share lot, one ticket at ₹92 is ₹46,000; a ₹5 lakh reference rounds down to 10 lots/₹4.60 lakh or up to 11 lots/₹5.06 lakh. The August 2022 prospectus lot was 1,000 shares. As a historical sensitivity only, corresponding bounds are 5 lots/₹4.60 lakh or 6 lots/₹5.52 lakh. Daily whole-lot capacity is floor(volume×participation/lot). At 2% or 5%, both tested lots yield zero whole lots on every observed row, whose largest volume is 5,000 shares. At 10%, the verified 500-share lot allows only 1 lot across the 5 known 20-window rows and 2 lots across the 26 known 60-window rows; the historical 1,000-share lot allows none. This is a conditional observed-row result, not proof of zero liquidity on unknown dates. No fictitious finite liquidation time is reported. [S5, S10, S14–S18]

Non-promoter shares at 31 March are 503,084, or 29.92% of capital, an upper bound on freely trading float, not verified accessible supply. The master supplies a dated price range and eligibility status, but spread, depth, comprehensive surveillance restrictions and executable bids remain ND. G4 Hold and L NS are appropriate; an unsupported numeric L1 would conceal the missing evidence.
